concepts.name: What affects Azure cost
concepts.description: Azure cost depends on several variables.

concepts.name: Azure Pricing Calculator
concepts.description: The Azure Pricing Calculator is a web tool for estimating the cost of a planned Azure solution before or while you design it.

concepts.name: Microsoft Cost Management
concepts.description: Microsoft Cost Management provides tools to analyze Azure costs, monitor spending patterns, create budgets, and help organizations control cloud spend.

concepts.name: Azure tags
concepts.description: An Azure tag is a key-value metadata label applied to supported Azure resources, resource groups, and some other scopes.

concepts.name: Microsoft Purview
concepts.description: Microsoft Purview provides data governance, data-security, and compliance capabilities that help organizations understand, govern, and protect data across their data estate.

concepts.name: Azure Policy
concepts.description: Azure Policy evaluates Azure resources and actions against organizational rules.

concepts.name: Resource locks
concepts.description: A resource lock protects Azure control-plane resources from accidental deletion or modification even when a user otherwise has permission.

concepts.name: Tags, Policy, locks, and RBAC solve different problems
concepts.description: Tags are metadata labels, Azure Policy evaluates resource compliance, resource locks block specified control-plane changes, and Azure RBAC grants management permissions.

concepts.name: Azure portal
concepts.description: The Azure portal is a browser-based graphical interface for creating, configuring, and monitoring Azure resources and services.

concepts.name: Cloud Shell, Azure CLI, and Azure PowerShell
concepts.description: Azure Cloud Shell is a browser-accessible shell environment for managing Azure.

concepts.name: Azure Arc
concepts.description: Azure Arc extends Azure management and governance capabilities to supported resources outside Azure, including on-premises and other-cloud environments.

concepts.name: Infrastructure as code (IaC)
concepts.description: Infrastructure as code (IaC) defines infrastructure in machine-readable files.

concepts.name: Azure Resource Manager (ARM)
concepts.description: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) is Azure's management and deployment layer.

concepts.name: ARM templates
concepts.description: An ARM template is a declarative JSON file that describes Azure resources and their desired configuration.

concepts.name: Azure Advisor
concepts.description: Azure Advisor analyzes supported Azure resources and provides personalized recommendations to improve areas such as reliability, security, performance, cost, and operational excellence.

concepts.name: Azure Monitor
concepts.description: Azure Monitor is Azure's monitoring platform for collecting, analyzing, and acting on telemetry from applications, infrastructure, and Azure services.

concepts.name: Log Analytics
concepts.description: Log Analytics is the Azure Monitor experience for querying and analyzing log data stored in a Log Analytics workspace.

concepts.name: Azure Service Health
concepts.description: Azure Service Health reports Azure service incidents, planned maintenance, and health advisories.

concepts.name: Azure Monitor alerts
concepts.description: An Azure Monitor alert watches telemetry or resource conditions and becomes active when an authored rule is met.

concepts.name: Application Insights
concepts.description: Application Insights is an Azure Monitor capability for application performance monitoring.

concepts.name: Advisor, Service Health, and Azure Monitor
concepts.description: Azure Advisor recommends improvements, Azure Service Health reports Azure platform events relevant to you, and Azure Monitor collects and analyzes operational telemetry.

questions.prompt: Which THREE factors can directly affect Azure cost?
questions.explanation: Azure cost depends on factors such as service/resource choice, usage, region, and pricing options. Organizational display choices do not directly set service price.
hints: Choose factors tied to what is deployed, how much is used, or where/how it is priced.

questions.prompt: A company wants Azure to audit or restrict resource configurations that do not meet organizational standards. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: Azure Policy evaluates Azure resource configurations against rules and can audit or enforce organizational standards at assigned scopes.
hints: Look for configuration compliance or enforcement.

questions.prompt: Classify each resource lock by what it protects against.
questions.explanation: A delete lock blocks deletion while allowing authorized modification. A read-only lock prevents changes and deletion through the resource-management plane.
hints: ReadOnly is more restrictive than a delete lock.

questions.prompt: A team stores desired infrastructure definitions in version control and repeatedly deploys environments from those definitions. Which practice is this?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code defines infrastructure in machine-readable files so deployments can be repeatable, reviewable, and automated.
hints: Definitions in version control and repeatable deployment point to IaC.

choice_feedback.b: Portal configuration can manage resources, but repeated desired-state definitions in version control are the IaC clue.
choice_feedback.c: CLI commands can be automated, but one-off interactive administration is not the described versioned declarative practice.
